title: The HPS sample size changes across 2024 cycles
caption: The nine cycles contain 610,755 respondent records. Cycle 9 has 51,280, compared with 68,544 in Cycle 1. These are survey sample sizes, not changes in the number of adults in the population. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS 2024 respondent CSVs; measured raw row counts.

title: State unemployment rose sharply in 2020, then declined
caption: The selected states' 2020 peaks were California 16.1% (Apr); New York 16.7% (May); Texas 12.8% (Apr); Virginia 11.9% (Apr). The shaded area marks March–December 2020; the timing alone does not identify a causal effect.
source: Source: BLS LAUS; seasonally adjusted monthly statewide rates.

title: Hardship differs across work and household income groups
caption: In Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16), the highest displayed hardship estimate is 55.8% for Worked in last 7 days / Under $50k. Income is the prior year's household income; did not work is broader than unemployment. Error bars show 90% intervals. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; U.S. adults with valid responses; PWEIGHT and 80 person replicates.

title: Adults facing expense difficulty report more loneliness and anxiety
caption: In Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16), frequent loneliness is 21.0% in the harder-to-pay group versus 8.2% in the other group; frequent anxiety symptoms are 26.9% versus 9.7%. These are descriptive comparisons, with 90% intervals; they do not show that hardship caused either outcome. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; national weighted valid responses within each hardship group.

title: Does lower state unemployment go with less financial hardship?
caption: Across 51 jurisdictions in Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16), the descriptive Spearman rank association is 0.10. Using the midpoint month instead gives 0.13. Dashed lines are state medians, not official thresholds. Each dot is a state or D.C.; the relationship is ecological and its sampling uncertainty is not shown here. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Sources: Census HPS state estimates joined to BLS LAUS using state FIPS and aligned collection periods.

title: Not every state returned to its 2019 unemployment rate
caption: 21 of 51 jurisdictions had a published 2024 annual unemployment rate at or below their 2019 rate. Changes range from -2.3 to +1.4 percentage points. A recovered rate does not mean every household recovered; each state has equal weight in this histogram.
source: Source: BLS LAUS; published unadjusted annual average unemployment rates, 2019 and 2024.

title: How loneliness and lack of support differ by age group
caption: In Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16), nationally 21.2% of adults aged 18-34 report frequent loneliness versus 6.2% of those 65 and older; lack of support is 47.9% versus 26.9%. State groups have as few as 124 valid answers, so their 90% intervals overlap in many comparisons. Differences between groups are not tested here, and the percentages describe survey self-reports, not diagnoses or the same people over time. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; adults with valid responses; PWEIGHT and 80 person replicates; 90% intervals.

title: Annual recovery rates and the monthly 2020 peak
caption: 21 of 51 jurisdictions have published 2024 annual rates at or below 2019. Calculations compare integer tenths to preserve exact ties and ±0.1-point boundaries. The separate rounding band does not change this exact rule. The sortable companion table includes all tied peak months, count and percent changes, and separate declining-employment/labor-force flags. BLS sampling intervals are not present in these exports.
source: Source: BLS LAUS; annual M13 values unadjusted, monthly peaks seasonally adjusted; counts in persons.

caption: Cycle 9: all 51 overall-state estimates pass the project rule. Order is descriptive. Interval overlap is not a test of equality, difference, or rank. A state and the U.S. estimate share respondents. No state-vs-U.S. significance categories are assigned. All cycles' estimates, sample sizes, missingness and flags are exported in the Round 1 follow-up tables. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; person weights and 80 replicates. The U.S. and state estimates are not independent.

title: Unemployment and hardship across states: uncertainty and stability
caption: In Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16) the rank correlation is 0.10 (90% resampling range -0.15 to 0.34). Across the nine cycles it ranges from 0.10 to 0.21, and the band includes zero in 9 of 9 cycles. The vertical bars show that each state's hardship estimate is itself uncertain. The shaded range resamples the 51 jurisdictions as if they were exchangeable. It is a descriptive sensitivity analysis, not a survey-design confidence interval or proof of no association. HPS sampling error, LAUS model uncertainty, and cross-cycle covariance are not captured. No causal or individual relationship is established. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Sources: Census HPS state estimates joined to BLS LAUS using state FIPS and aligned collection periods.

title: Do states that recovered less also report more hardship?
caption: In Cycle 9 (2024-08-20 to 2024-09-16), 14 of 51 jurisdictions had unemployment at or below their 2019 level for the same months. The rank correlation between the change in unemployment and hardship is -0.06 (90% resampling range -0.27 to 0.16); for the unemployment level (Chart 10) it is 0.10. Hardship in 2019 is unknown, so this does not show whether hardship changed. Each dot is a state; the pattern is ecological and says nothing about individuals. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Sources: Census HPS state estimates; BLS LAUS unadjusted rates, aligned cycle months vs the same months of 2019.

title: National measures stay in a narrow range across 2024 cycles
caption: National estimates move within narrow ranges: hardship 35.7% (cycle 3) to 37.4% (cycle 7), loneliness 13.0% (cycle 9) to 13.9% (cycle 2), lack of support 40.0% (cycle 4) to 41.0% (cycle 9) and anxiety symptoms 15.4% (cycle 1) to 16.3% (cycle 2). Each cycle is a new cross-section, and the raw sample falls from 68,544 to 51,280 respondents, which can widen the intervals. Whether cross-cycle differences are real is not tested here. Phase 4.2 added prepaid wireless numbers at Cycle 8; the contribution to the missingness drop is unknown. Changes are not service-demand changes. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS, all U.S. adults with valid answers to each question; PWEIGHT and 80 replicates; 90% intervals.

title: Missing answers and state sample sizes
caption: Household income is the most often missing answer (14.4% to 18.5% across cycles), and it is kept as unknown, not as low income. The expense question is missing for 5.4% to 11.2% (highest in cycle 3). Missing answers to the expense question fall from 10.6% in cycle 7 to 5.4% in cycle 8, with similar drops for the other questions, Census documents the addition of prepaid wireless numbers to the Phase 4.2 contact frame at Cycle 8 and warns about comparability. This does not identify why the observed item missingness fell. The smallest state sample is North Dakota in cycle 9 with 347 valid answers. Between 7% and 15% of state-by-age loneliness estimates are suppressed, depending on the cycle. Missing answers may differ from the answers we see, and weights only partly adjust for that. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS 2024 respondent files (missingness) and weighted state aggregates (valid counts).

title: Matching HPS cycles to LAUS months: sensitivity check
caption: The two matching rules differ by at most 0.48 percentage points (Rhode Island, cycle 9), and the rank correlations differ by at most 0.03 in any cycle. The differences are largest in cycle 9, where the aligned rate exceeds the midpoint-month rate in 98% of states. Both rules give weak correlations, and both describe the state, not the respondents. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Sources: Census HPS cycle dates; BLS LAUS unadjusted monthly state rates.

title: Hardship by work status and household income, all 2024 cycles
caption: Adults who worked in the last 7 days report more hardship than adults who did not work in every band and cycle. In cycle 9 the gap is 5.2, 13.0 and 4.1 points in the three bands. The difference between income bands is much larger: working adults under $50k are 36.4 points above working adults at $100k+. 'Did not work' is broader than unemployed, and household income is not the person's own income. National results only. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; U.S. adults with valid answers; PWEIGHT and 80 replicates; 90% intervals.

title: Loneliness and anxiety by expense difficulty, all 2024 cycles
caption: Adults with somewhat/very difficult expenses report more frequent loneliness (22.7% in cycle 1, 21.0% in cycle 9) than the other group (8.3% and 8.2%) and more frequent anxiety symptoms (26.5% and 26.9% versus 9.5% and 9.7%). The gap between the two groups is at least 12.9 points in every cycle. These are survey self-reports, not diagnoses, and they do not show that hardship causes either outcome. Missing/invalid HPS answers are excluded per outcome; valid n, Kish effective n, missing n and suppression flags are supplied in the accompanying evidence tables.
source: Source: Census HPS; national weighted valid responses within each hardship group; 90% intervals.
